videos.title: Rwanda to Host F1’s Return to Africa, Will It Pay Off?
videos.description:
Rwanda has been chosen to host Formula 1’s return to Africa, beating competition from South Africa and Morocco. With the first Grand Prix planned for the early 2030s, the country is betting on a new circuit, airport and hotels to drive tourism, create jobs and boost its economy. But can the benefits justify the cost? On Bloomberg’s Next Africa, Jennifer Zabasajja speaks to Rwanda’s Sports Minister Nelly Mukazayire about funding, jobs and the country’s sporting ambitions. Sports economist Victor Matheson examines the potential returns and how much revenue could stay in Rwanda, while FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem discusses the winning bid, affordability and the possibility of more African races. Bloomberg’s Loni Prinsloo looks at the reaction across the continent, South Africa’s disappointment and the infrastructure challenges ahead.

Chapters:
00:00:00 - Formula 1’s return to Africa
00:01:18 - South Africa misses out
00:04:12 - Rwanda’s sports minister on the F1 plan
00:09:15 - Can the Grand Prix pay off?
00:14:53 - FIA president on F1’s future in Africa
00:19:58 - Funding, infrastructure and Africa’s reaction

videos.title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Turn Up at China Site Tied to Alice Huang
videos.description:
A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. 
The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News.
Bloomberg's Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney get details from Olivia Levieux, Markets Strategist with Bloomberg News

videos.title: How Cuba’s Population Collapse Is Making Its Crisis Worse | WSJ
videos.description:
While conditions in Cuba deteriorate due to mounting U.S. sanctions, a fuel embargo, and a failing state apparatus, another, potentially even more catastrophic problem looms: the island’s population is shrinking at an alarmingly rapid rate. The population loss, which some researchers estimate could amount to a full quarter of the island’s inhabitants over a mere five-year stretch, is virtually unprecedented for a country that isn’t at war. And it has enormous implications for both Cuba’s present and future. 

WSJ traveled to the island to see firsthand how its mass exodus is changing daily life in the country, and complicating any hopes of a turnaround.

videos.title: HBCUs and the World Bank Group: A Global Partnership
videos.description:
A Shared Mission, A Global Vision for Transforming Lives and Strengthening Economies

What happens when two institutions with a shared commitment to transforming lives and communities come together to advance global development?

Historically Black Colleges and Universities have a distinguished legacy of developing global leaders, advancing scientific discovery, fostering entrepreneurship, and driving economic and social transformation in the United States and around the world. Building on this legacy, collaboration brings together HBCUs' talent, research capabilities, innovation, and global networks with the World Bank Group's development expertise and global reach to create jobs, strengthen economies, and advance shared development priorities.

In this conversation, IFC Vice President Elena Bourganskaia and Xavier University of Louisiana President Dr. C. Reynold Verret explore how the World Bank Group and HBCUs can leverage education, innovation, and entrepreneurship to create jobs, strengthen economies, and expand opportunity, building on a legacy of service and translating shared commitments into lasting development impact.
